Our Ir(III) complexes emit green to orange photoluminescence in polystyrene film, with λPL in the range from 529 nm for Ir-H to 583 nm for Ir-CN and with unity photoluminescence quantum yield.

title: Towards Reactive Electrochemical Transport Using the Lattice Boltzmann Method. Part II: Atomistically Informed Non-Ideal Species Transport
abstract: The lattice Boltzmann method (LBM) provides an efficient framework for simulating species transport in electrochemical systems; however, conventional formulations commonly rely on ideal or dilute-solution descriptions that neglect molecular-scale non-idealities near solid–electrolyte interfaces. In this work, we extend our previously developed LBM formulation to incorporate non-ideal thermodynamic contributions through the excess chemical potential.

title: Online Soil Column Chromatography Coupled with Mass Spectrometry for Studying Sorption of Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances and Other Organic Contaminants
ShapeAligner: Direct Molecular Superposition from Clique-Based Atom Correspondence
abstract: Superposing one small molecule onto another is routine in ligand-based drug discovery. In atom-level correspondence methods, the pose the correspondence determines is only a starting point, and a subsequent search produces what is reported. We present ShapeAligner, a rigid aligner whose output pose is the superposition its maximal clique correspondence determines. Maximal cliques of an association graph over chemically typed heavy atoms each fix a reflection-free, equally weighted Kabsch transform in closed form. An analytic Gaussian shape-and-color volume overlap ranks the resulting poses.

title: Interpretable Processing–Structure Relationships in Spirulina Bioplastics through Automated Spectral and Microstructural Analysis
abstract: Algal bioplastics are emerging as a promising class of sustainable materials, but their development is limited by an incomplete understanding of how processing governs structure. Establishing principles connecting processing to structure is hindered by manual analysis and the complexity of structural data. Here thermomechanical processing conditions (time, temperature, and pressing force) are mapped to structural descriptors of Limnospira platensis (spirulina) bioplastics.

title: Temporal Programming of Interfacial States Reveals a Hidden Formate Pathway from CO2 Reduction on Palladium
abstract: Controlling electrocatalytic selectivity requires not only tuning catalyst composition but also controlling the interfacial states that emerge during operation. Here, using bulk Pd as a model system for electrochemical CO 2 reduction reaction (CO 2 RR), we show that poor steady-state formate production emerges from time-dependent evolution of the electrochemical interface. Pd initially exhibits appreciable formate activity but rapidly accumulates strongly bound CO and evolves toward a CO-rich, formate-inactive state.

title: Extensive A-Site Magnesium Solubility in Perovskite Oxides via Precursor-mediated Synthesis Pathways
abstract: Incorporation of Mg 2+ on the A-site of ABO 3 perovskite oxides such as BaTiO 3 and SrTiO 3 has been limited by severe ionic size differences of the A-site cations with some reports claiming <1% substitution possible. Here, we demonstrate a precursor-mediated synthesis pathway to achieve extensive A-site Mg 2+ substitution in perovskite oxides – up to 50 mol%. By leveraging binary and ternary metal carbonates that are chemically mixed at the crystallographic scale, barriers associated with conventional solid-state reactions are bypassed.

title: Spiral-Growth-Induced Nanosteps on Layered Oxyhalide Photocatalysts Enhance Anisotropic Charge Separation for Visible-Light Water Splitting
abstract: Layered mixed-anion compounds are promising photocatalysts for solar fuel production owing to their visible-light absorption and suitable band-edge positions. However, their two-dimensional crystal structures hinder the spatial separation of reduction and oxidation sites because both photogenerated electrons and holes predominantly migrate in-plane along the layered frameworks. In particular, in plate-like particles reflecting this layered structure, charge carriers must travel relatively long lateral distances.

title: Incorporating Computational Chemistry into Introductory Courses with a No-cost, Installation-free Molecular Dynamics Activity in Python
abstract: Molecular simulations have become indispensable in applications ranging from drug discovery to materials design and battery technology, yet students are typically not exposed to these techniques until upper-level physical chemistry courses towards the end of their undergraduate education. This late exposure to computational chemistry can limit opportunities for students to develop proficiency or participate in faculty-led computational chemistry research.

title: THIOETHERS AS POTENTIAL ANTIBACTERIAL AGENTS AGAINST METHICILLIN-RESISTANT STAPHYLOCOCCUS AUREUS (MRSA)
abstract: The emergence and rapid spread of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) have created an urgent need for new antibacterial agents capable of overcoming established resistance mechanisms. Among the diverse sulfur-containing scaffolds, thioethers have attracted increasing attention because of their structural versatility and ability to modulate antibacterial activity through incorporation into different pharmacophores.

title: Fatigue, Memory and Training in Thermo-Responsive Hydrogels
abstract: Responsive materials are a cornerstone of functional soft matter. Their functionality relies on switching between equilibrium states, a process generally assumed fully reversible over repeated cycles. Here we show that thermo-responsive hydrogels can instead develop progressive fatigue and irreversibility during repeated volume phase transitions. Viscoelastic phase separation generates mechanical stresses that drive permanent network rearrangements and trap phase-separated morphologies, creating a non-volatile structural memory.

title: Coupled Thermal Activation and Autocatalytic Cure Kinetics: A Theoretical and Computational Study of Delayed Reactive Transformation
abstract: The delayed transformation of a reactive material into a solid phase is limited, in most thermal-management approaches, by a basic trade-off between transport stability and transformation speed. We formulate and computationally analyze a coupled zero-dimensional model in which (i) a lumped thermal energy balance governs the fluid element's temperature, including exothermic self-heating from the reaction itself; (ii) the release of a reaction-triggering species follows a physically motivated first-order relaxation toward a temperature dependent, Arrhenius-rate-controlled saturation level (a…

title: Vicem: Automating Molecular Mechanics Modeling of Solvation Dynamics with Applications to Time-Resolved X-ray Scattering
abstract: Time-resolved X-ray solution scattering (trXSS) probes molecular-scale structural dynamics in solution, but its interpretation requires efficient computational methodologies and models for assessing how changes in solute structure and charge distribution affect the surrounding solvent shell and the resulting scattering signal. We present VICEM, an OpenMM/ASE-based software suite for constructing solvated molecular models, running molecular dynamics simulations, inspecting and analyzing the resulting trajectories, while exposing solute geometry, partial charges, Lennard–Jones parameters, and…

title: A molecular sewing machine
abstract: Living molecular architectures adapt and evolve by continuously exchanging energy with their surroundings. To mimic this behavior, synthetic tools have been developed to switch 25 artificial systems between states; however, these systems generally relax toward thermodynamically inert equilibria. Creating “life-like” synthetic materials that operate far from equilibrium therefore remains a major challenge.

title: Decoupling additive manufacturing from virgin resource consumption through recyclable bio-composites
abstract: Additive manufacturing could support decentralised, on-demand production, but it remains largely reliant on linear polymer systems that consume virgin resources and generate persistent waste. Here, we report a fully bio-derived composite platform for closed-loop additive manufacturing based on dynamic lipoic acid networks and renewable fillers. Printable inks containing hydroxyapatite or thiol-functionalized silica were processed by direct ink writing to produce robust three-dimensional structures.
